messages:
alex: Quick follow-up from the dedicated GPU orchestration RFC — I want to propose a 'lease-proxy' pattern that separates fast, soft prewarm leases from the strong allocation lease. Goal: reduce cold-start latency without over-committing billing/eviction surface.

maria: OK, sketch the invariants. How do we avoid double-counting headroom and accidental over-provisioning?

alex: Invariants I'm thinking: 1) soft lease = ephemeral, not billed to tenant; holds warm cache + weights, can be revoked anytime. 2) promote -> strong lease when request arrives and headroom available. 3) only one promoted strong lease per tenant slot. 4) soft leases can be shared across compatible model families.

jonathan: Sounds reasonable. Two tradeoffs: cross-tenant soft sharing reduces cold starts but increases eviction complexity; promotions must be cheap. Also need a clear metric to decide when to promote vs serve with fallback model.

riley: Telemetry will be critical. Emit events: soft_lease_acquire, soft_lease_evict, soft_lease_promote, promote_latency_ms, promote_failures. We can then baseline promotion P95 and tune heuristics.

maria: Billing note: we should bill only after promotion (i.e., when the strong lease is created and GPU is attached). Otherwise customers will be confused. Also need audit logs for promotions to satisfy compliance requests.

alex: Agreed. Admission control: the proxy should gate promotions with a token bucket per-pool + per-tenant rate limit to prevent stampedes. If promote fails we either fallback to: a) queued promote, b) serve from hosted model, or c) degrade quality. Configurable per-tenant policy.

jonathan: Operator boundary question: where does the proxy run? Two options: a) control-plane sidecar (centralized) b) operator-local sidecar (per-node). I prefer control-plane for global headroom visibility, but it increases blast radius if proxy goes down.

alex: I'm leaning control-plane for now. We can run the proxy as a replicated service with leader election and local caching to reduce RTTs. Keep operator primitives minimal: strong lease CRD + soft-lease annotation that the proxy manages.

jonathan: Example config I had in mind (very rough):
```
leaseProxy:
  mode: control-plane
  promoteRatePerTenant: 2/s
  sharedSoftPools: ["llama-2-13b","redwood-verified-13b"]
  billingOnPromote: true
```

riley: Tests: synthetic burst with 500 tenants, 2% promoted per second; assert promote latency < 200ms P95, promote-fail rate < 0.5%. Also chaos tests where proxy loses leader and recovers.

maria: Rollout plan: feature-flag behind org opt-in, canary in one region and then expand. Add a toggle to switch between control-plane vs local proxy for experimentation.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout triggered for lease-proxy v0.3 to cluster-gamma :rocket:

alex: Next steps: I'll draft a short RFC follow-up doc with sequence diagrams and state machine for enqueue/promote/evict. Volunteers for owner/implementer? (I can own the follow-up writeup).

jonathan: I can take the operator CRD + controller integration.

riley: I'll own telemetry/alerting spec and test harness.

maria: I'll own rollout/checklist and billing/audit hooks.

alex: Great. I'll convert this thread into the RFC follow-up and ping eng-sre and product for feedback. :thumbsup:
